plan: Run 3-state, 4-state, 6-state HCM fits sequentially. Then compare AIC. Then parameter sweep all three.

3state.notes: k_off at hard lower bound (p=0.000, 10 s⁻¹). k_1=0.34 low — 3-state lacks power stroke dynamics. ΔAIC vs 6-state = +1577 → worst model.

4state.notes: k_off near lower bound (p=0.019). Good fit. ΔAIC vs 6-state = -4.48 → loses to 6-state.

6state.notes: WINNER. k_on at upper bound (p=0.9998, ~1e8) — FLAG FOR PI. k_9 at lower bound (1 s⁻¹) — titin pathway engaged. k_1=1.11 s⁻¹ HCM-plausible (~4x control).

aic_comparison.interpretation: 6-state wins with ΔAIC=4.48 vs 4-state (moderate support, >2 threshold). 3-state ruled out (ΔAIC=1577).

sweep_results.key_finding: k_1 is the dominant HCM force driver across ALL models: 46× force increase over sweep range (6-state). k_9 (titin coupling) contributes <1% to peak force — titin pathway engaged by fitting but not a peak-force driver. k_off (Ca deactivation) is second most sensitive: lower k_off → more force AND more SRX depletion (more activation).
sweep_results.for_julia: Primary input to heart geometry model: k_1 (SRX exit rate). HCM fitted value: 1.11 s⁻¹ (~4x estimated control ~0.3 s⁻¹). This drives SRX→DRX transition, increasing attached crossbridges and peak force. At HCM k_1 value, SRX drops from ~99.9% to ~99.2% during activation — small but highly nonlinear in force output.

sweep_all_results.method: All kinetic params swept at x0.1, x0.316, x1.0, x3.16, x10 of best-fit value. Zero-valued params (k_8, k_10) swept from baseline=0.01. Run 2026-05-18.

cross_model_findings.universal_drivers: k_1 (SRX exit), k_3 (attachment), k_on (Ca activation) — positive in all models. k_2 (SRX entry), k_4_0 (detachment), k_off (Ca deactivation) — strong inverse in all models.
cross_model_findings.k_6_0_finding: Reverse power stroke (k_6_0, k_6_1) has ZERO effect on peak force in both 4-state and 6-state — model is insensitive to back-stroke rate. Can be fixed or removed.
cross_model_findings.titin_specific: 6-state titin params k_8, k_9, k_10, k_13, k_14 all <1-2% effect. k_11/k_12 (vertical DRX transitions) have modest ~2x effect.
cross_model_findings.hcm_mechanism_for_julia: k_1 (SRX exit rate): best-fit 1.11 s⁻¹ in HCM vs ~0.3 s⁻¹ control. Increasing k_1 from 0.1x to 10x of HCM value gives 334→36140 N/m² (108x range). This is THE primary force-driving knob.
cross_model_findings.p710r_paper_consistency: P710R paper (Vander Roest 2021): 12.9x increase in k_-SRX (=k_1). Our H251N fit shows ~3.7x increase. Both confirm SRX disruption as primary HCM mechanism.
